processing: Little is documented about this estate's manufacture; Maskeliya gardens are generally known for orthodox western high-grown black tea.
harvest_season: Picked through the year, as on other Sri Lankan estates; little is recorded about its best season.
appearance_dry: Typical of high-grown Ceylon: dark brown broken leaf.
appearance_liquor: Typical of the district: clear, bright reddish amber.
appearance_wet: Coppery brown broken leaf, as with other western high-grown teas.
taste_profile: No tasting record exists for this garden; as with other western high-grown Ceylon teas, expect a brisk, clean cup.

brewing.notes: Western-style, as with most Ceylon black tea.

vintage_note: Its own sales are little documented. Usual for its class: sold by grade and invoice, best within a year or two of manufacture.
description:
Gartmore is a tea estate name from the Maskeliya district, in the hills near Adam's Peak. Very little is documented about it as a tea in its own right.

The fair comparison is its district. Maskeliya is known for western high-grown black tea of traditional orthodox make, so a Gartmore invoice would be expected to sit in that family, though nothing confirms a house style.

Brew it as you would other Ceylon black tea, Western-style with water just off the boil, and judge the actual lot rather than the name.
history: Little is documented about when Gartmore was opened, who ran it or how its tea has changed.
